Care · programme

Medical Mission

Volunteer physicians, specialists and health professionals from the US and Palestine building long-term health capacity in Palestine: prosthetics, eye and cancer screening, hospital equipment and workforce training.

Branch
Care · Destinations
Owning entity
Unconfirmed: the deep dives and the prototype say ARFHSN (the Human Services Network); Program Architecture's money map still says AFRP or an entity to confirm.
Shape
Mission · flagship
Built in the Hub
Designed

Who it's for

Health professionals as volunteers, and donors. Credential requirements for volunteers are not published.

The operating year

A report session at the Convention; credential expiry surfaced 90 days out; trustees report to the AFRP Board every six months. Mission dates are not stated.

The five rungs

RungFor this programme
HearA health professional who consents to show their occupation to programme committees.
Show upThe annual report session at the Convention; no follow-up is queued.
Take partTravelling on a mission, gated on current licence, cover and Ministry of Health authorisation.
Give or serveGiving or serving, ranked equally: a gift receipted by ARFHSN, or hosting and teaching trainees. The most populated rung.
LeadA seat on the ARFHSN Board of Trustees, elected by the AFRP Board.

Who runs it

The Medical Mission Committee within ARFHSN; ARFHSN's 14-seat Board of Trustees is elected by the AFRP Board and reports to it every six months.

Money

Restricted gifts and a conduit routed through HQ (11.1.5). Gifts must be receipted in ARFHSN's name under a recorded inter-entity agreement.

Hand-offs

Fed by RBPN's professional directory and the Convention. Project Hope delegations visit mission sites; Women to Women is its sister programme.
